youtube_title: Wanatah, Indiana: the petrified woman, an 1891 newspaper hoax (Wanatah request)
youtube:
You asked for Wanatah! In 1891, a newspaper story said a young woman who had vanished from her father's home, two miles south of Wanatah, around 1851 had been found 40 years later in an abandoned bog-iron pit, turned to stone. It was a hoax: Indiana's Lincoln Highway Byway says a local newsman, Harry Darling, concocted it, and the Wanatah Historical Society calls it just a story. It still made a splash. Papers as far away as North Carolina reprinted it, and the historical society tells of people coming by train to see her, only to be told there was no petrified woman. Comment your town, and it could be next! #Wanatah #LaPorteCounty #Indiana #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn, and no woman is shown, because there never was one. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: Wanatah Historical Society, "The Petrified Woman of Wanatah" (from the Valparaiso Star, May 29, 1891); Indiana's Lincoln Highway Byway turn-by-turn guide, 1928 route east (2024); 1891 reprints in The Montgomery Vidette (Troy, N.C., June 11) and the Watauga Democrat (Boone, N.C., June 25), via DigitalNC. You asked for Wanatah!
In 1891, a newspaper story said a young woman had vanished from her father's home, two miles south of Wanatah, around 1851.
Forty years later, it said, she was found in an abandoned bog-iron pit. The iron in the water had turned her to stone.
But it was a hoax. There was no petrified woman. Indiana's Lincoln Highway Byway says a local newsman, Harry Darling, made it up.
It still caused a stir. Papers as far away as North Carolina reprinted it, and the Wanatah Historical Society tells of people coming by train to see her, only to be told there was no petrified woman.
